children: Gold futures fall to their lowest level since late August of 2025 as the rout continues amid concerns that the Fed will continue raising interest rates. The Anthropic IPO and its subsequent start of trading contributed to this week's selling in gold and bitcoin, but for gold the bigger factor is interest rates, says Mauricio Di Bartolomeo, co-founder of bitcoin-backed lender Ledn. "A quarter-point hike on Dec. 9 is all but a given, cash pays over 4% and the 10-year pays over 5%, so [gold] holders sitting on big gains can lock in yield and wait to buy back lower." Front month gold falls 4.6% in New York to $3,512.30 a troy ounce, and silver falls 7.4% to $41.035 a troy ounce, for weekly losses of 9.5% and 16%, respectively. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
